newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sumitomo may withdraw from Malaysian copper market.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo may withdraw from Malaysian copper market.

text.p: Malaysian cable makers said on Tuesday they were prepared for a halt in supply of refined copper from Japan's Sumitomo Corp, following talk the company was backing out of the Thai market from next year.

Senior industry executives in Malaysia said Sumitomo, however, only supplied 10 to 15 percent of the 160,000 tonnes of copper cathode needed in the country annually and this could be sourced elsewhere.
"They've not given any indication they will supply us with copper cathode next year and I think they'll discontinue," said a top official of a listed copper cable firm in Kuala Lumpur.
Another cable company executive in Kuala Lumpur said the withdrawal of Sumitomo, which has suffered massive copper trading losses this year, will not hurt the Malaysian market for refined copper.
"We get our supply of copper cathode from the US, Zambia, Chile, Australia, the Philippines and Japan and this is ample at the moment," said the executive.
Bangkok Cable Co president and chief executive Sompong Nakorsri said on Tuesday he did not expect the Thai copper market to receive any supplies from Sumitomo next year.
Traders in Japan acknowledged this and also talk that Sumitomo was cutting back in other markets.
Officials at Sumitomo's regional office in Singapore were not immediately available for comment.
